Rumors suggest Apple will offer two distinct new models for MacBook Pro users this fall: a MacBook Pro with the M6 chip, and an all-new MacBook Ultra. Here's an overview of what's coming.

The M6 MacBook Pro and MacBook Ultra are both set to debut this fall, each with its own unique strengths

Apple is expected to launch two new Macs this fall, both catching the eye of MacBook Pro users:

  • MacBook Pro with M6 chip
  • MacBook Ultra (possibly still called MacBook Pro)

The MacBook Pro with M6 chip is expected to succeed last fall's M5 model, offering no higher-tier chip options and no external redesign.

The M6 chip, however, looks to be an exciting, larger-than-usual upgrade, as it will be the first Mac chip built on a 2nm process. For users who love the current MacBook Pro design—plenty of ports and outstanding battery life—keeping the existing design could be a selling point.

If MacBook Pro users want something more distinctive, the MacBook Ultra might be just the ticket.

The rumored Ultra model will reportedly feature an all-new industrial design, a thinner and lighter body, and an OLED display, touchscreen, Dynamic Island, and possibly even cellular connectivity options.

The MacBook Ultra will not use the M6 chip, instead offering M5 Pro and M5 Max versions. Still, for any user chasing the most cutting-edge technology in a Mac, the MacBook Ultra will have the answers beyond just the chip.

Based on Apple's past Mac release cadence, the M6 MacBook Pro and MacBook Ultra are expected to arrive in late October. However, if you need a new MacBook Pro right now or are on a tight budget, Apple's refurbished offerings or Amazon deals are also worth considering.

Are you planning to upgrade your Mac this fall? Which new model has caught your eye? Let us know in the comments.
